subject: english
title: The Verb Time Machine — Infinitive, Simple Past, Past Participle
subtitle: The sequel to Verb Engine, and the teaching deck behind the Irregular Verbs reference list. Why English has three verb forms where Japanese has two, and what the third one is actually for. 26 slides · 4 guided practices · 10-question formative assessment · soccer and movie examples throughout.

content: Name the three forms of an English verb and explain why English needs three where Japanese uses two.
Choose the right form using the two tests — is there a helper word, and does the sentence say WHEN.
Sort irregular verbs into pattern families rather than memorizing all of them one at a time.
language: Use the simple past for a finished action that names its time, standing alone with no helper: scored, went, ate.
Use the past participle for its two jobs — have/has + participle for the present perfect, and be + participle for the passive.
Return the main verb to the infinitive after did / didn't, so only one word in the sentence carries the past.
